parts:

messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Identifying Parent BranchPoint of EndPoint
parts: I am an undergraduate student at UCLA and have been finding your package very useful.
Thanks for your interest in nat. Glad to hear that it has been useful.
This may seem like a simple question but could you tell me how to obtain the BranchPoint Parent of an Endpoint, in other words, the beginning and end of a branch?

There are a lot of ways to do this but none of them are currently a single step. The best way depends on the details of your use case. I suggest that you take a look at the documentation for the segmentgraph function, which simplifies a neuron to its branch and end point only : 
and take a look at this package vignette
http://natverse.org/nat/articles/neurons-as-graph.html

In particular I have updated this vignette section to include a sample approach to your problem.`

http://natverse.org/nat/articles/neurons-as-graph.html#segment-graph
May I also ask how End and Branch points are identified from an .swc file with only PointNo, Label, X, Y, Z, and Parent? I very much appreciate your help.

The Parent column defines the full connectivity graph including end and branch points implicitly:

* All points except the root have a parent (the root node has parent -1 to indicate this)
* A child is a point that has a given point as its parent. 
* An End point has a parent but no children 
* A Branch point has multiple parents or multiple children

Best wishes,

Greg Jefferis.
